text:
maya: FYI support escalated — customer AC reports dramatic p99 API latency from EU around 09:20 UTC. They see responses taking an extra ~600-900ms. Reports suggest requests are detouring via US before landing on EU POP. :rotating_light:

sasha: can we get a correlation id + trace sample? which EU POPs? any recent infra changes? @kevin @rod

maya: correlation id cid=ac-2024-09-04-8743. affected: eu-west, eu-central. recent change: reduced GSLB TTL 60s->10s at ~08:55 for PD testing (ticket PD-442).

kevin: pasted a sanitized traceroute from customer probe to our eu-west POP:
traceroute to api.redwood.example (eu-west-pop) 30 hops max
 1 isp-gw 1.2 ms
 2 transit-a 8.4 ms
 3 us-west-peering 98.5 ms  <- unexpected detour
 4 us-west-agg 99.2 ms
 5 eu-west-pop 15.6 ms

kevin: that extra hop explains ~80-100ms added latency (plus TLS handshake).

ops-bot: Incident alert: edge-routing-anomaly detected (p99 latency EU) — alert_id=IR-4873 — created 1709998765

rod: can we verify GSLB answers briefly contained us-west IPs for EU prefixes? run dig from multiple vantage points.

sasha: running dig against gslb01 from EU and AP probes (raw):
# vantage: EU probe
$ dig +short @gslb01 api.redwood.example A
203.0.113.12

# vantage: AP probe
$ dig +short @gslb01 api.redwood.example A
198.51.100.22

sasha: EU probe got 203.0.113.12 which maps to a us-west node IP. so mapping mismatch during ttl churn.

maya: mitigation plan (immediate):
- rollback DNS TTL to 60s (undo 10s change) to stop rapid pool churn
- tilt GSLB weights to favor eu endpoints until propagation completes
- enable canary probes to verify p95/p99 across EU pops for 30m
- mid-term: add short affinity window (sticky by ASN/CIDR) to avoid flips when TTL < 30s

ops-bot: Action scheduled: rollback-gslb-ttl -> 10s -> 60s. apply at 1709998820. change id cdn-config-01.

kevin: example curl TLS timings I collected to illustrate handshake overhead:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_pretransfer:%{time_pretransfer} time_total:%{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health

kevin: sample when hairpinning occurred:
# time_connect:0.098 time_pretransfer:0.110 time_total:0.980
force-eu-ip directly:
# time_connect:0.016 time_pretransfer:0.018 time_total:0.120

carla: ops, consider enabling TLS session ticket reuse on edge POPs to reduce handshake CPU/RTT cost for high-QPS clients. file a change if needed.

rod: ops-bot reports rollback applied at 1709998820. starting canary probes now. waiting ~TTL window for full propagation.

sasha: canary results t+2m after rollback: eu-west p99 down from ~980ms -> ~170ms. p95 ~60-90ms. path/tls timings look normal. continuing 15m monitor.

maya: solid. next actions: (1) follow up with GSLB team to prevent multiregion answers on rapid TTL churn, (2) add auto-alert when DNS answers disagree with client ASN, (3) if recurrence, open postmortem. i'll draft a customer-facing summary and timeline.

kevin: opened runbook PR "gslb-quick-rollback" with exact CLI steps and sanity checks.

carla: +1 on auto-alerting and session ticket reuse. also recommend a small traffic holdback for 2m after any GSLB TTL change to reduce flip storm.

maya: leaving this thread open until 1709999350 to confirm stability. thanks all. :pray:
